clue.text: Plenty to eat, but won't it go round?

definitions.text: Plenty to eat, but won't it go round?

parts.words: Plenty to eat, but won't it go round?
parts.note: a hearty, filling dinner is described by a phrase that also names a four-sided shape, and a square shape cannot roll or go round

explanation.definitionFit: A filling, substantial dinner is idiomatically called by this name, and the shape word in it cannot be round.

clue.text: Protection, say, going round iron model

indicators.note: the word say goes round, enclosing the other pieces, so it is the container here

parts.note: taken as written
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
the Model T was Ford's famous car, so model gives T

explanation.surface: Someone describes a protective iron model.
explanation.walkthrough: The Model T Ford is so famous that 'model' alone stands for its letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Protection and security from harm are both senses of this word, as in a guard rail fitted for protection.

clue.text: One French male and all the others creating a disturbance

parts.note: un is the masculine French word for one
the rest means all the remaining ones

explanation.surface: A Frenchman and everyone else cause a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrest is a state of agitation or discontent, the political sense of a disturbance.

parts.note: rump steak is a cut of beef
a parliament is a legislative house

explanation.surface: A diner at Westminster asks about the steakhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rump Parliament sat at Westminster in 1648-53 after Pride's Purge, so Westminster is a loose, allusive definition; 'steak, house' reads as steakhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: The remnant English legislature of 1648-53 met at the Palace of Westminster.

definitions.meaning: a very small person, read as minute plus man

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it is a tiny person, a dwarf; as one word it is an American intercontinental ballistic missile.

parts.note: cute means attractive in a dainty way

explanation.surface: Someone praises a charming way of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accent' is the written mark over a vowel, not a way of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: The acute is a diacritic mark, a stroke slanting up over a letter as in café.

clue.text: This could be the reason why I didn't walk out

definitions.text: This could be the reason why I didn't walk out

parts.words: This could be the reason why I didn't walk out
parts.note: read as staying indoors because of the weather rather than leaving a meeting in protest

explanation.definitionFit: Wet weather falling from clouds is a common reason for not going out for a stroll.

indicators.note: fluttering suggests letters moving about restlessly, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bird flaps about near a target, that is.
explanation.definitionFit: An egret is a heron, and this word is another name for that bird as well as its plume.

parts.note: port means the left-hand side, so a car's port side, the side nearest the kerb in Britain, is meant, not a garage shelter

explanation.definitionFit: In Britain the left side of a vehicle is next to the kerb, the nautical port side.

parts.note: a second is a moment of time, so a celebrity for a second is someone currently famous

explanation.definitionFit: A phrase for the person everyone is talking about right now, with a moment being a second.

clue.text: Return of drink in the marketplace

indicators.note: return means the following word of is turned back to front

parts.note: rum is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: Someone brings back a drink in the market square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the marketplace' reads as where the drink is drunk, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Rome the public square used for trade and assemblies was called by this Latin word.

clue.text: Complaint that could be painful to face

definitions.text: Complaint that could be painful to face

parts.words: Complaint that could be painful to face
parts.note: a complaint is an illness here, and the facial nerve pain it causes is literally painful in the face, not hard to confront

explanation.definitionFit: Trigeminal nerve pain is a well-known ailment causing sharp pain in the face.

clue.text: One drunkard or another returning to the place

indicators.note: returning means the word for another drunkard is read backwards

parts.note: another drunkard is a sot
a spot is a place

explanation.surface: One drinker or another heads back to the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' means another drunkard, and 'returning' turns that word back before the place.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a habitual heavy drinker, from tossing back a pot of ale.

clue.text: They go off to the match

definitions.text: They go off to the match

parts.words: They go off to the match
parts.note: the match is a marriage, not a football game, and they go off secretly to be wed

explanation.definitionFit: Couples who run away together to marry in secret are known by this term.

parts.note: an act planned in advance, as in a deliberate crime, is described

explanation.definitionFit: Something planned beforehand and deliberate, as in a crime thought out in advance.

parts.note: the famous novel's black horse suggests a black steed, while the phrase means an unexpected winner

explanation.walkthrough: Black Beauty is Anna Sewell's novel about a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a horse of a dark colour; idiomatically an outsider who surprises by winning.

clue.text: From IOM, Edgar used symbol to represent a word

indicators.note: used signals the letters are taken and worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Edgar from the Isle of Man adopted a sign standing for a word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used' rearranges IOMEDGAR; IOM is the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: A character such as a Chinese logogram that stands for an idea or word rather than a sound.

clue.text: Shrill and harsh like an owl?

definitions.meaning: a barn owl gives a piercing cry rather than a hoot

explanation.definitionFit: A piercing, grating sound is described by this adjective, as is the call of the barn owl.

clue.text: Sign language first in the books

indicators.note: language first tells us the word for language goes before the sign

parts.note: diction is a choice of words or language
Aries is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Sign language comes first in the reading list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sign language' reads as signing for the deaf, but sign is the star sign and 'first' moves language to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Reference books listing words with their meanings.

indicators.note: magic suggests the letters are transformed as if by a spell

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A clergyman belongs to the Magic Circle, the magicians' club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Magic' rearranges CIRCLE; the Magic Circle is a British society of conjurors.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister of religion is a member of the clergy.

clue.text: Part held by schemer generally to come into view

indicators.note: part held by says a portion of the next words is kept within them

explanation.surface: A scheming person generally emerges in public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part held by' points into schEMER GEnerally.
explanation.definitionFit: To appear from hiding or become visible.

definitions.meaning: in cricket a bowler delivers an over
to staff with more workers than needed

explanation.definitionFit: A cricket bowler delivers each over, so is whimsically an over-man; as a verb it means to put excess staff on.

indicators.note: taken by means the point is received into the word nice

parts.note: E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A pleasant relative scores a point.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's daughter is a family relation.

clue.text: Gangster Robin left with word of hesitation

parts.note: Robin Hood is the legendary outlaw
um is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A gangster called Robin leaves, saying um.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent criminal or thug.

indicators.note: disturbed means the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Our troubled man from Crete tells tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone skilled at telling anecdotes entertainingly.

indicators.note: gave us means the word Terrorists supplies these letters from within it

explanation.walkthrough: 'gave us' signals the run inside tERRORists; 'the slip' sounds like an escape.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip is a mistake or blunder.

parts.note: May is a month, here part of a date
a day numbered zero, O, makes the date impossible

explanation.surface: Someone describes a date that could never happen in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: May the nought-th, MAY plus O for zero, is a date that cannot exist; 'in Ireland' defines the county.
explanation.definitionFit: A county in the west of the Republic, so a place found in Ireland.
